To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified mutations in a gene called CCDC114 that causes a disease called ciliary dysmotitly and primary ciliary dyskenesia.

we used exome sequencing to determine that mutations in a new PCD gene, CCDC114, are a cause of PCD, and to further demonstrate the utility exome sequencing to find genetic causes of PCD and other recessive disorders.

exome sequencing of six individuals with primary ciliary dyskenesia (PCD, a genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive disorder) with outer dynein arms (ODA) mutations identified mutations in six genes, including two known PCD genes and a new PCD gene, CCDC114.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of primary ciliary dysfunction (PCD), a rare genetic disease that is characterized by chronic respiratory infections, infertility and situs abnormalities.

the identification of genes that cause Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia, a genetically heterogeneous, recessive disease that is characterized by oto-sinopulmonary disease and, in some individuals, situs abnormalities.
the molecular basis of human genetic disease and the identification of novel genes and pathways that are involved in the etiology of human disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCDC114 mutations are a cause of PCD.
mutations in CCDD114 are a cause for PCD and ciliary dysmotilities.
mutations in CCED114 are a cause for ciliary dyskinesis and primary ciliary dysgenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified mutations in CCDC14 as a cause of PCD.
we identified mutations in CCDC 114 as a new gene causing PCD and that exome sequencing is useful to identify new genes causing PCD.
we have identified CCDC114 as an additional gene associated with PCD and have shown the utility of exomic sequencing in identifying the genetic cause of a heterogeneous disorder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to identify mutations in a gene that was not previously known to cause PDC.
mutations in CCCD114 are a cause for cilia dysfunction.
we have identified CCDC114 as the cause of PCD.
